title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 239
paragraphs: If, however, having found fault with the opinions proposed by others, I am bound to declare an opinion of my own on these matters in doubt, I will tell what to my mind is the reason why the Nile increases in summer. In the winter season the Sun, being driven away from his former path through the heavens by the stormy winds, comes to the upper parts of Libya. If one would set forth the matter in the shortest way, all has now been said; for whatever region this god approaches most closely and stands directly above, that region may reasonably be supposed to be most in want of water, and its native streams of rivers are most dried up.
